Fig. 1.
Illustration of the on-ramp merging scenario. The AV on the ramp
lane needs to safely and efficiently merge into the main lane.
Fig. 2. Overview of our method, SARMI, consisting of a high-level decision-making layer (left) and a low-level motion planning layer (right).

Fig. 3. The policy update process primarily involves the actor network, reward critic network, cost critic network, as well as the AMM and ASM. The solid
line indicates the process of the RL agent interacting with the environment to generate experiences, whereas the dashed line represents the process of the RL
agent updating network parameters by utilizing mini-batches sampled from the replay buffer.

Fig. 4. Illustration of the prediction-based action shielding mechanism. EV
denotes the ego vehicle, and SV denotes the surrounding vehicle.

Fig. 5. Kinematic bicycle model. XOY and SOD represent the Cartesian and
Frenet coordinate systems. The reference line is the lane centerline.
Fig. 6. Comparative study. (a) Average reward, (b) Average cost, (c) Crash ratio; the shaded region denotes the standard deviation across five random seeds.

Fig. 7.
Visualization of the testing performance of the trained SARMI method under different traffic density conditions. The green box denotes the ego
vehicle. We also show the historical trajectory of the ego vehicle.

Fig. 8. Comparison of passenger comfort between MPC and PID at the low-
level motion planning layer. For clarity, traffic density levels are denoted as L
(low), M (medium), and H (high). Longitudinally, MPC achieves performance
comparable to PID. In the lateral direction, MPC outperforms PID.

Fig. 9. The training results of the ablation study, structured with four groups: the full SARMI, SARMI w/o ALM, SARMI w/o ALM and AMM, and SARMI
w/o ALM, AMM, and ASM. ALM (Augmented Lagrangian Method), AMM (Action Masking Mechanism), ASM (Action Shielding Mechanism).
Fig. 10. Training results of the ablation study on the risk field term.

Fig. 11. Illustration of the NGSIM US-101 merging scenario. The green vehi-
cle represents the ego vehicle, while the yellow vehicles denote surrounding
vehicles. The transparent rectangles in front of each vehicle indicate their
predicted future trajectories.
